questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to study volcanoes and geothermal systems, which Iceland has many of, and the University of Iceland teaches classes about it at the right time of year and in English. The university also has a very similar general system to the University of Copenhagen, which helped streamline everything.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As a geology student, I was insufficiently prepared for how math-intensive the seismology course and the continuum mechanics and heat transfer course were. I ended up spending a lot more time reading up on mathematics than I expected.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy, once I did as instructed and obtained a student ID I quickly found out how to navigate the university website. I still can't make it work on my phone though, it won't let me log in for some reason.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I asked for directions to where I could get a student ID, went there and got one along with some info on how to use it and the university email, and then used it as instructed to find my schedule. It turned out three of my courses overlapped, so I had to drop one and take another as well take one as a mainly book course, but that was fairly simple.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was difficult to find anything within an acceptable price range online, but in the end it turned out that my mother's colleague had a friend in Reykjavik who was renting rooms for a reasonable price. Generally, expect everything to be very expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's really expensive. Other than that, I had it pretty easy - the room I rented was very close to the university, and general amenities were available in the house.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would have liked to be able to live in campus housing, but due to a registration mishap I was too late to find any housing for individual students. I found a facebook group that was talking about doing a roommate thing, but it didn't go anywhere. More rooms or single apartments would have been nice.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Probably my fault, but at first I signed up with the email for my home university. This caused me to not show up as registered at all until I got worried about not having received any updates and mailed the host university. The one who was supposed to take care of such things was on vacation, so I had to wait another two weeks before my acceptance was verified. The rest was very easy.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: After applying through Mobility Online those of us who were nominated began receiving emails and webinar invites regarding the registration process and what to expect on arrival. Included in this was a link to the application site, where we then applied to the host university. Those of us who were accepted then had to get a student ID from the help desk upon arrival.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We were encouraged to ask questions during the webinars or send them to the host university's contact person. Unfortunately she went on vacation just before I asked about my application, but calling the university's general call center did at least clarify what had happened. After arriving, there was someone at the student help desk who got me a student ID and a paper with general information.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Three of the classes I first picked overlapped, so I had to change one and take another as a book course. In hindsight I am glad that I took the new course, but I am still pretty disappointed at not being able to attend most lectures from the other.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read the instructions carefully, sign up for student housing very quickly, and don't use you home university's email for the application.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Two of my courses were much more math-heavy than I expected, but I think they were technically intended for geophysicists and not geology students like myself. They were also mixed BA and MA.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Two of my courses were mixed BA and MA, while the other two were BA only. Those two had a lot of high-level math I understood little of.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Generally similar, just much more math and less labwork.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Volcanology, Geothermal energy, Seismology, Continuum mechanics and heat transfer.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them were good, seismology and continuum mechanics and heat transfer were very difficult though.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing really, everything was just a lot more expensive than I am used to.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Pretty much everything was more expensive than I expected, but especially the food.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were some fun parties, although a lot of it was at nightclubs which really aren't my scene. There were some other tours, but I never saw the announcements about them before it was too late to sign up.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Parties and a couple of festivals

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I heard that the film festival was good, although I caught a cold that week and didn't participate.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Definitively check out the hot springs and glaciers, the outdoor swimming pools are also very nice to visit with some friends

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, hardest part was accepting that all hot water here smells of sulfur.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Show up to the parties?

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Stinky hot water

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Lots of hot water (the outdoor swimming pools are very nice).

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Expect matrices and differential equations if you pick a course involving math
2. Make sure you check for messages often - they are not always timely
3. Remember to have fun?

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to sign up for student housing as soon as possible

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I have now walked on a glacier, made some new friends, and seen a geyser. I have also learned a lot.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Math. So much math.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
